requirements.evidence: Entities table with named slug index and soft deletes (database/migrations/2026_10_29_000000_create_entities_table.php:14-20); memberships with cascading FKs, role default, both named unique indexes and the generated owner_seq (database/migrations/2026_10_29_000001_create_entity_memberships_table.php:14-36); all contract members present: Entity (app/Models/Entity.php:14,45,55,63,73), EntityMembership scopes/relations (app/Models/EntityMembership.php:25-73), UserRole with manageable() (app/Models/UserRole.php:5-18), User relations/membershipFor (app/Models/User.php:37-56), factories with states (database/factories/EntityMembershipFactory.php:33-58), both policies with argument-free constructors and bool returns (app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:9-57, app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:7-50). Docs updated as required (docs/database-schema.md:4, replacing the owner_membership_id note; CHANGELOG.md:9,15).

conventions.evidence: Policies are the only authorization path and are auto-discoverable for the models (app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php, app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php); deliberate mass-assignment via #[Fillable] (app/Models/Entity.php:14, app/Models/EntityMembership.php:13) matching the existing User model; generated-style reversible migrations with docblocks and down() (database/migrations/2026_10_29_000001_create_entity_memberships_table.php:28-48); Pest feature test (tests/Feature/EntityModelTest.php:9); docs kept in sync (CHANGELOG.md:9,15, docs/README.md:12, docs/database-schema.md:4,138,151-154,165). No new service/repository layer.

security.evidence: Every ability derives from the caller's own membership row, never from client input (app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:22,51-55, app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:14,44-48), owner membership is protected from deletion (app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:31-33), and generated owner_seq is hidden from serialization (app/Models/EntityMembership.php:14). Remaining gap: assignRole checks only the caller's role, so an admin may change the owner's membership or assign the Owner role; UserRole::manageable() (app/Models/UserRole.php:16) is not enforced by this change.

tests.evidence: Tests cover the DB one-owner invariant (tests/Feature/EntityModelTest.php:51-55), multiple owners across entities (58-68), all three scopes (31-40), owner relation (42-49), both pivot directions plus membershipFor (70-76), and positive/negative cases for every policy ability (78-125). Missing: no test for UserRole::manageable() (app/Models/UserRole.php:16), no test for entity soft deletes or rejection of a duplicate slug.

simplicity.evidence: Lean change that reuses User::membershipFor instead of new query layers (app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:42, app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:46) and no speculative abstractions. Minor duplication: the owner-or-admin lookup exists twice (app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:51-55, app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:44-48).

readability.evidence: Small focused methods with one-line docblocks and full type hints (app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:14-55, app/Models/EntityMembership.php:52-73); names mirror the task vocabulary (owner/admin/employee); matches sibling style in app/Models/User.php.

scope.evidence: Only models, enum, factories, migrations, policies, tests and the two docs the conventions/task require (CHANGELOG.md:9,15, docs/database-schema.md, docs/README.md:12). No routes, Livewire components, session handling or other out-of-scope features.

issues.explanation: assignRole only checks that the caller is owner/admin; it neither excludes the owner's membership nor restricts the target role to UserRole::manageable(), so an admin can demote the owner or hand out ownership unless every future write path remembers to intersect with manageable().
Contract behaviour UserRole::manageable() (and entity soft deletes / duplicate-slug rejection) ships without a test, although every other requirement is covered.
The owner-or-admin membership lookup is duplicated in both policies; a single method on User (next to membershipFor) would remove the copy-paste.
The test named 'creates entities with a unique slug' only asserts the slug is non-empty and never proves a duplicate slug is rejected, despite the unique index being the point.
membershipFor issues a fresh query on every policy check (two or three times per ability), which will repeat identical lookups within one request; caching the result per entity id would be cheap.

review.summary: The change implements the entity/membership data model end to end: migrations with the portable generated owner_seq and its unique index, models, enum, factories, both policies, Pest coverage of the DB invariant and every ability, plus the required doc updates. The implementation matches the contract closely and is well scoped; the remaining points are a minor authorization nuance around assigning roles to the owner, a couple of untested contract details, and a duplicated helper, so it is approvable with nits.
